findings.detail: D1 [confidence; verdict final sentences; remainingUncertainty item on E15] Draft 2 lowers overall confidence from 'high' to 'moderate' and gives one label for two different conclusions. The verdict itself says the rejection rests on VERIFIED/CORROBORATED evidence (E1, E2, E6, E13) and that only the replacement recommendation (setup-node caching, E15 INFERRED) and parts of the hardening advice are weaker. A single 'moderate' label could make a decision-maker think the reject decision is less certain than the evidence shows, when the action is sending NPM_TOKEN/CLOUD_DEPLOY_KEY off the runner. The draft should state confidence separately: high for 'do not adopt @v2 / 9f3e0b1 in release.yml', moderate for the specific replacement and hardening details.
